transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Lyndi Kenyon.
President Trump leaves today for a summit in Asia.
NPR's Anthony Kuhn reports this summit will include an unprecedented three-way meeting
Thursday with the leaders of Russia and China.
Trump's first stop is Manila, the Philippines, where he will attend a summit of the Association
of Southeast Asian Nations, or ASEAN.
From there, it's on to the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen, for an Asia-Pacific Economic
Cooperation Organization summit.
Trump has said he wants to negotiate a new arms control deal with Russia and China, but
China, which has the smallest nuclear arsenal of the three, is not likely to be interested.
Trump will also try to extend a truce in the U.S.'s trade war with China.
Trump's critics are concerned that Trump could side with Russia's Vladimir Putin and China's
Xi Jinping in deciding the fate of smaller actors such as Ukraine and Taiwan without
their participation or consent.
Anthony Kuhn in PR News, Seoul.
The now former head of NVIDIA has recently gained support for his return to the company
after resigning just last week.
NPR's Rick Mulvey explains.
There's a petition for Jensen to return.
It has over 120,000 signatures, including support from Elon Musk and, according to the
petition's website, about 6,000 current NVIDIA employees.
Don't forget, Jensen Wong made a lot of people a lot of money over the long term.
Jensen Wong, who was the CEO of the computer chip company, resigned amid revelations over
multiple affairs.
One of those affairs allegedly involved a woman whom U.S. intelligence officials claimed
to be spying for China.
Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland will challenge Senator Chuck Schumer to become the
new Senate Majority Leader.
Both have decades of experience on Capitol Hill.
NPR's Eric McDaniel has the story.
Schumer's been in elected office in Washington for 45 years, Van Hollen for about 25.
But the Maryland Democrat, who's run Democrats' campaign efforts in both chambers and is a
former deputy to Speaker Nancy Pelosi, is positioning himself as a change candidate.
He's got some high-profile backers in his corner, including Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan
and Bernie Sanders of Vermont, but he'll need nearly 30 Democrats in a secret ballot vote
to get across the finish line.
For now, leader Schumer's projecting confidence.
He's led Democrats for a decade and said he has the support necessary to secure reelection
as leader.
Eric McDaniel, NPR News Washington.
That collision last week between a riverboat cruise ship and a tanker on the Mississippi
River appears to be due to what is being termed a "steering casualty."
NTSB investigator Bard Barnum described the finding.
The Atlantic asphalt was upbound on the Mississippi River in the proximity of the Crescent City
Connection Bridge.
It experienced the steering casualty resulting in the rudder remaining to starboard.
All 100 people aboard were safely evacuated.
This is NPR.
This weekend, Citi Field, home of the New York Mets, hosted the sixth annual New York
bagel fest, thousands of people attended, including reporter Jeff London.
Who doesn't love a doughy, chewy bagel?
Over 50 vendors from New York City, across the United States, and even abroad attended
this year's event, handing out samples from their kitchens to an appreciative crowd which
voted for their favorite bagels.
Professionals did, too, and at the end of the day, a winner was crowned.
The 2026 New York Bagel Fest Best Bagel Award goes to Esa Bagel!
At the local company with several outlets in Manhattan and Brooklyn is celebrating its
fiftieth anniversary this year, and the win was the schmear on the top of the bagel.
For NPR News, I'm Jeff London in New York.
Triple A says pricey plane tickets and expensive gasoline are expected to keep some Americans
from traveling for Thanksgiving this year.
The auto club estimates about 121,000 fewer people will travel domestically between the
Tuesday before Thanksgiving and the Monday after.
If the projection proves true, it would represent a one-tenth of one percent decline from 2025
and would end three years of record Thanksgiving travel following the COVID pandemic.
Triple A prepared its forecast weeks before problems with U.S. air traffic control communications
on Friday that prompted a nationwide ground stop.
I'm Lynda Kenyon, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: Trump departs for Asia summit, with a possible three-way meeting with Russia and China Thursday
NVIDIA petition backs former CEO Jensen Huang's return after resignation over multiple affairs
Senator Chris Van Hollen to challenge Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leadership
Mississippi River riverboat cruise ship and tanker collision blamed on steering casualty; all 100 evacuated
New York Bagel Fest at Citi Field crowns Esa Bagel as best bagel of 2026
AAA projects slight decline in Thanksgiving travel, citing high airfares and gasoline prices
